solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Soak, eating cold northern dish

indicators.note: one word eating another takes it inside itself, so the cold letter goes within

parts.note: to souse is to soak or drench
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone drenching themselves while tucking into a hearty dish from the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Scouse is a meat-and-vegetable stew associated with Liverpool, in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Scouse is a stew traditionally eaten in Liverpool, a regional dish of northern England.

clue.text: Book weak defender

parts.note: soft can mean weak or lacking firmness
a back is a defending player in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A literary review dismissing a feeble footballer who plays in defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A softback is a paperback, a book bound in flexible covers.

clue.text: Getting better, working with those people on objective

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed on another sits above it, so these letters come before the objective

parts.note: on means operating or working, as a machine is on
them refers to those people
an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: A recovering patient busy with others, focused on a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone recovering from illness or a situation improving.

clue.text: Area of London covered by Waterloo hospital from the east

indicators.note: reading from the east, in a down clue as in an across one, means reading the letters backwards
the letters wanted are covered by the phrase, sitting inside it across the word break

explanation.surface: A London district said to be near Waterloo and served by its hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'covered' into the definition, leaving the hidden word with no signal; 'covered by' is the hiding indicator. The run OHOS spans waterlOO HOSpital and is turned back by 'from the east'.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district of the West End of London, famous for nightlife and restaurants.

clue.text: Plan to relax mostly in historic French city

parts.note: a chart is a plan or map

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for relax is dropped

parts.note: to rest is to relax

explanation.surface: A holiday planner deciding to unwind for most of a trip to an old French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the T from REST to leave RES.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartres is a cathedral city southwest of Paris with a long medieval history.

clue.text: Tilt and extract what's left of drink

parts.note: a ship heels when it tilts to one side
to tap is to draw off or extract liquid, as from a barrel

explanation.surface: Tipping a glass and draining the dregs from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A heeltap is the small amount of liquor remaining at the bottom of a glass.

clue.text: Range of new report covering energy quashes anger

indicators.note: in a down entry a piece that quashes another sits on top of it, so the anger comes after
the rearranged letters cover, or enclose, the energy letter
new suggests the letters of report are made afresh in another order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A fresh report on power supply suppresses public fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quashes' works by position: in a down answer the first part sits on top of, and so squashes, the second. 'new' gives REPRTO, which 'covering' wraps round the energy letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A repertoire is the full range of works or skills a performer has available.

clue.text: Firm's truck in the US needing identification

parts.note: in American usage a rig is a large truck

explanation.surface: A company's lorry, stopped in America, requiring papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a noun meaning a company; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid means stiff and unbending, the adjectival sense of firm.

clue.text: Scream from one being eaten by green ogre?

indicators.note: something eaten by another ends up inside it, so the one goes within the ogre

parts.note: Shrek is the green ogre of the animated films
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The cry of a victim being devoured by a green monster.
explanation.definitionFit: A shriek is a loud, high-pitched cry, the same as a scream.

clue.text: Popular party with men over the threshold

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a do is a party or celebration
OR, other ranks, is the military term for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A well-liked gathering with guests stepping across the doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Something past the threshold of a building is inside it, under a roof rather than outside.

clue.text: Possibility of getting drunk — fetch a can!

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger out of place, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drinker demanding a can of beer as the chance of intoxication beckons.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is used ironically: it really means almost no possibility at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom ironically names a likelihood, said when the speaker means there is very little chance.

clue.text: Empty gesture welcomed by standard caller

indicators.note: something welcomed by another is taken in, so it goes inside

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level

indicators.note: an empty word has its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A hollow gesture received by a caller of typical kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caller' is not a visitor at the door but a device that calls; 'Empty' keeps only the outside letters of the gesture word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager is a bleeper that calls its wearer, alerting them to get in touch.

clue.text: Complaint from busy worker (female)

parts.note: the bee is proverbially busy, and worker bees do the hive's labour

explanation.surface: A grievance raised by a hardworking woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is informal for a grumble or grievance.

clue.text: Crossing to pay for game of cards

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay it
bridge is a card game for four players

explanation.surface: A wager crossing over into paying up for a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestrian bridge is a crossing over a road, river or railway for people on foot.

clue.text: Early enough to welcome panel with extra minutes to play

indicators.note: one phrase welcoming another takes it in, so the panel goes inside

parts.note: arriving in time means early enough
a jury is a panel of people giving a verdict

explanation.surface: Arriving promptly to greet the judges, with time to spare before a game.
explanation.walkthrough: In football, time added at the end of a half for stoppages is called injury time.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoppage time added on at the end of a football half lets the remaining minutes be played.

clue.text: List in church ending prayer daily

indicators.note: the leaning word goes in the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a ship lists or leans to one side

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A roster in a church, finishing with the daily prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' looks like an adverb; in British usage a daily is a domestic cleaner who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a daily is a char or housekeeper who cleans someone's home regularly.

clue.text: The last letter in copra possibly gives you an anti-depressant

indicators.note: the letter goes in the rearranged word
possibly signals the letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A curious claim that a coconut product, plus one letter, becomes medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges COPRA to PROAC, and 'in' sets Z inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Prozac is the brand name of fluoxetine, a widely prescribed antidepressant drug.

clue.text: Compensation for wrong agreed and intended to be broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken aloud, so the words give a sound

parts.note: at one means in agreement, and meant means intended; together they say at-one-meant

explanation.surface: Reparation for an offence, agreed and meant to be announced publicly.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonement is making amends or reparation for a sin or offence.

clue.text: Love comes between truth and the belly for such a dogsbody

indicators.note: the letter comes between the two words, sitting where they meet

parts.note: a fact is a truth
tum is informal for the belly
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A romantic notion wedged between honesty and appetite for a lowly servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is an employee who does all kinds of jobs, the same as a general drudge.

clue.text: A day merely to adapt

parts.note: just means merely or only

explanation.surface: A single day is all it takes to get used to something.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust is to change to suit new conditions, the same as adapting.

clue.text: Weapon made of explosive containing free energy

indicators.note: the explosive holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: TNT is the explosive trinitrotoluene
to rid is to free from something
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A weapon built from explosives with some untapped energy packed in.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear, a weapon associated with Neptune.

clue.text: Brazilian accountants taking in their city?

indicators.note: the accountants take the city in, holding it between them

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant, so two of them give the letters twice
Rio de Janeiro is the city of Brazilians, and of this answer in particular

explanation.surface: A group of Brazilian accountants visiting their own city.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'their' refers to the answer: Rio is the city of the Brazilians the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: A carioca is a native of Rio de Janeiro, so a particular kind of Brazilian.

clue.text: Copper salesman's strike

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a tout is a pushy salesman, as of tickets

explanation.surface: A policeman's hawker friend, or a walkout by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer; here it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike something out is to delete or remove it, which is to excise it with a snip.

clue.text: Women supply weapons and regularly dump exercises

parts.note: to arm is to supply with weapons

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: Women equipping themselves and routinely dropping their workouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of dump, U and P.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm-up is a set of light exercises done before strenuous activity.

clue.text: Choke, seeing criminal pay his tax due at last

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter

explanation.surface: A tax evader is so enraged by a bill that he nearly chokes.
explanation.definitionFit: To asphyxiate is to suffocate, as when someone chokes for lack of air.

clue.text: People chasing son trapped by model

indicators.note: something trapped by another is held inside it

parts.note: to pose is to model, as for an artist

explanation.surface: A pursuing crowd and a boy caught out by a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a band of people pursuing a fugitive, as in Westerns.

clue.text: Experienced in soft fabric

definitions.meaning: to have ... something is to have experienced it
a matted, pressed woollen cloth, soft to the touch

explanation.surface: Someone well-versed in soft materials.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the past tense of sensing or undergoing; the other is a pressed wool cloth.

clue.text: Almost reject incentive

indicators.note: almost means not quite the whole word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: to spurn is to reject

explanation.surface: A motivation one nearly turns down.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is something urging one on, a stimulus or incentive.

clue.text: Language mostly principal across South America

indicators.note: the shortened word spreads across, enclosing, the abbreviation for South America
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for principal is dropped

parts.note: main means principal or chief

explanation.surface: A tongue spoken in much of South America, mostly the main one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts MAIN to MAI, which goes 'across' SA. The surface points to Spanish or Portuguese, but Masai is East African.
explanation.definitionFit: Masai is the tongue of the Masai people of Kenya and Tanzania, also called Maa.

clue.text: Rig pressure absorbed by strangely quiet men

indicators.note: something absorbed by another is taken into it
strangely signals the letters appear in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Fixing an outcome by pressure on oddly silent men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges QUIET MEN to EQUIMENT, and P is absorbed into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rig as a noun means gear or apparatus, such as a drilling rig or fishing tackle.

clue.text: Puts a block on public relations occasions

parts.note: events are occasions

explanation.surface: A spin doctor blocking the staging of publicity events.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something is to stop it from happening, to obstruct it.

clue.text: For the time being metro is out of order after onset of problems

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the first letter
the onset of a word is its first letter
out of order means not in the proper arrangement, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The underground railway is temporarily broken, causing problems.
explanation.walkthrough: The metro looks like the broken subject of the surface, but it is the anagram fodder; 'out of order' shuffles it to ROTEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro tem is short for the Latin pro tempore, meaning temporarily.
